# How to Price Your Minis


It can be hard to judge how much your collection is worth. Now, Miniswap gives you the tools you need to cut out the guesswork.


We built our price history tool by aggregating sold listing data from eBay and Miniswap, matching it against Miniswap's product catalogue, and analyzing each sold listing's contents, assembly and painting status, so we could get a comprehensive view of how each variable affects realized prices compared to MSRP.


## Price history on every product


Price history is now displayed on each product page where we've gathered enough useful data. The Market Value card shows the median sold price for New in Box, On Sprue and Assembled copies of the kit, and the Price History chart shows how those prices have moved over time against MSRP.


We also suggest a price based on your listing information in the listing creation form, and listings priced well under market get a Good Deal badge so buyers can spot them.


## Market medians


The numbers below are medians: half of sales closed higher, half lower.


The numbers below are medians: half of sales closed higher, half lower.


- **New in Box kits converge at 85% of MSRP** , in line with manufacturer-specified minimum prices. Half of all sealed kits sell for *less* than that, so keep an eye out for deals by creating alerts on the products you want.
- **Painted units regularly sell for above MSRP, but only at the highest end.** Models listed as pro-painted, commission or display pieces go for a median 149% of MSRP, and three in four of them beat list price. Models described as tabletop standard or battle ready go for 80%, below what a sealed box fetches.
- **Primed and unpainted, assembled models average 65% of MSRP.** Primer makes no difference to the price. Partially painted models do slightly worse at 63%, and models that need stripping go for around 56%.
